# AirDropX protected local-server fork

Forked from `react-native-local-server@0.1.0` (ISC license); originally by dedydantry. Install as a local npm dependency: `"react-native-local-server": "file:vendor/react-native-local-server"`, then reinstall dependencies and rebuild both native apps. Changes in `node_modules` alone do not survive installs.

## Access contract

`start()` returns `http://<ip>:<port>/s/<48 lowercase hex chars>/`. The 192-bit capability is generated by the native platform CSPRNG after binding and is replaced on each stop/start. Do not strip the path when sharing the URL. The browser dashboard requests `files.json` and direct files **relative to this URL**; the mobile receiver must do the same. The only deliberately public endpoint is the exact `/airdropx/info` discovery file. Root `/`, `/files.json`, `/api/files`, `/api/dir`, `/download/*` and raw file URLs outside the capability prefix return 404. Even under the prefix, only the dashboard (`/s/<token>/`) and flat files are accessible; nested paths and directory listings are disabled. Native `isProtected()` allows JS to refuse to start on an older unprotected build.

Security scope: a bearer link on **unencrypted HTTP** protects against LAN clients that do not know the link; anyone who receives/observes it can download until the server stops. This is not paired-device approval or TLS. Prevent leaking the link through logs and external scripts. Changes require a native rebuild; JS-only updates cannot secure a previously built app.

## Smoke test on rebuilt Android/iOS device

With the server running and one shared file, confirm with `curl -i` that `/`, `/files.json`, `/<name>`, `/download/<name>`, `/api/files` and `/api/dir` each return 404; `/airdropx/info` returns 200; and `<QR-URL>files.json` and `<QR-URL><encoded-name>` return 200. Check encoded traversal (`%2e%2e%2f`, `%252e%252e%252f`) and mismatched tokens return 404. After leaving/re-entering the server screen, the old URL must return 404. Test the web dashboard and mobile receiver with the new QR URL.
